findings.title: A multi-region CloudTrail trail is enabled and logging management events
findings.description: Without an active multi-region trail, API activity in some regions is not recorded, leaving no audit trail for incident response.
findings.expected_state: At least one multi-region trail is logging and records read+write management events
remediation: CloudTrail > Trails > Create trail with 'Apply trail to all regions' enabled.
Record management events (Read and Write) and make sure logging is started.
In AWS Organizations, an organization trail satisfies this for all member accounts.

CIS.title: Ensure CloudTrail is enabled in all regions

findings.title: CloudTrail log file validation is enabled
findings.description: Digest files let you prove that log files were not modified or deleted after delivery.
findings.expected_state: LogFileValidationEnabled = true
remediation: CloudTrail > Trails > trail > General details > Edit > enable 'Log file validation'.

CIS.title: Ensure CloudTrail log file validation is enabled

findings.title: CloudTrail trail is integrated with CloudWatch Logs
findings.description: CloudWatch Logs integration enables near-real-time alerting on suspicious API activity. Delivery must be recent (within 24h).
findings.current_state: No CloudWatch Logs log group configured
findings.expected_state: Trail delivers to a CloudWatch Logs group and the latest delivery is < 24 hours old
remediation: CloudTrail > trail > CloudWatch Logs > Edit > enable and select/create a log group and IAM role.
Add metric filters and alarms for the CIS monitoring controls (root usage, console sign-in without MFA, etc.).

CIS.title: Ensure CloudTrail trails are integrated with CloudWatch Logs

findings.title: Security group does not expose SSH (22) to the internet

findings.title: EBS encryption by default is enabled in the region
findings.description: With the account-level default on, every new EBS volume and snapshot copy is encrypted automatically.
findings.expected_state: EBS encryption by default is enabled in every region
remediation: EC2 > Settings > Data protection and security > EBS encryption > Manage > Enable (repeat per region).

CIS.title: Ensure EBS Volume Encryption is Enabled in all Regions

findings.title: EBS volume is encrypted
findings.description: Unencrypted volumes expose data if snapshots are shared or the underlying media is mishandled.
findings.expected_state: Volume Encrypted = true
remediation: Snapshot the volume, copy the snapshot with encryption enabled, and create a new volume from it.
Swap the volume on the instance during a maintenance window, then delete the unencrypted volume/snapshots.

CIS.title: Ensure EBS Volume Encryption is Enabled in all Regions (volume-level evidence)

findings.title: Instance requires IMDSv2
findings.description: IMDSv1 is vulnerable to SSRF-based credential theft (e.g. the 2019 Capital One breach pattern).
findings.expected_state: Instance metadata option HttpTokens = required
remediation: EC2 > instance > Actions > Instance settings > Modify instance metadata options > IMDSv2 'Required'.
Set the account/region default for new instances to IMDSv2 required.

CIS.title: Ensure that EC2 Metadata Service only allows IMDSv2

findings.title: MFA is enabled for the root user
findings.description: The root user has unrestricted access to the account. Without MFA, a leaked password gives full account takeover.
findings.expected_state: Root user has an MFA device registered
remediation: Sign in as the root user and open Security credentials.
Under Multi-factor authentication (MFA), choose Assign MFA device and complete enrolment (prefer a hardware/FIDO2 key).
Store the root credentials and recovery material offline; use the root user only for tasks that require it.

CIS.title: Ensure MFA is enabled for the root user account

PCI_DSS.title: MFA for all access into the CDE

findings.title: No access keys exist for the root user
findings.description: Root access keys are long-lived credentials with unrestricted privileges and cannot be scoped down.
findings.expected_state: No root access keys
remediation: Sign in as the root user, open Security credentials > Access keys.
Make each root access key inactive, confirm nothing breaks, then delete it.
Use IAM roles / IAM Identity Center for programmatic access instead.

CIS.title: Ensure no root user account access key exists

findings.title: Root user does not use a virtual MFA device
findings.description: CIS recommends a hardware MFA device for root. The API exposes virtual MFA devices by serial number but cannot distinguish a hardware token from a FIDO2/passkey, so PASS means 'MFA present and not virtual'.
findings.current_state: Root MFA is not enabled at all
findings.expected_state: Root MFA is a hardware / FIDO2 device (not a virtual authenticator app)
remediation: Sign in as root > Security credentials > MFA.
Remove the virtual MFA device and register a hardware TOTP token or FIDO2 security key.

CIS.title: Ensure hardware MFA is enabled for the root user account

PCI_DSS.title: MFA for all access into the CDE

findings.title: MFA is enabled for all IAM users with a console password
findings.description: Console users without MFA are exposed to password phishing, reuse and brute force.
findings.current_state: Console password set but no MFA
findings.expected_state: Every IAM user with a console password has MFA active
remediation: IAM > Users > select the user > Security credentials > Assign MFA device.
Better: remove IAM console users and federate through IAM Identity Center with enforced MFA.

CIS.title: Ensure MFA is enabled for all IAM users that have a console password

PCI_DSS.title: MFA for all access into the CDE

findings.title: Active access keys are rotated within 90 days
findings.description: Long-lived access keys increase the window in which a leaked key can be abused.
findings.expected_state: Every active access key was created/rotated within the configured maximum age (default 90 days)
remediation: Create a second key for the user, update the application to use it, and verify.
Deactivate then delete the old key.
Prefer IAM roles with temporary credentials so no long-lived key exists.

CIS.title: Ensure access keys are rotated every 90 days or less

findings.title: Password policy requires a minimum length of 14
findings.description: Short passwords are easy to brute-force. Without a custom policy AWS defaults to 8 characters.
findings.expected_state: Account password policy minimum length >= 14 (configurable)
remediation: IAM > Account settings > Password policy > Edit, set minimum password length to 14 or more.

CIS.title: Ensure IAM password policy requires minimum length of 14 or greater

findings.title: Password policy prevents reuse of the last 24 passwords
findings.description: Allowing reuse undermines rotation: users cycle back to compromised passwords.
findings.expected_state: Password reuse prevention >= 24 (configurable)
remediation: IAM > Account settings > Password policy > Edit, enable 'Prevent password reuse' with 24 remembered passwords.

CIS.title: Ensure IAM password policy prevents password reuse

findings.title: Each IAM user has at most one active access key
findings.description: Multiple active keys per user widen the attack surface and often indicate skipped rotation clean-up.
findings.expected_state: At most one active access key per IAM user
remediation: Identify which key is in use (last-used date), then deactivate and delete the other.

CIS.title: Ensure there is only one active access key available for any single IAM user

findings.title: No attached customer-managed policy grants full "*:*" admin access
findings.description: Policies allowing Action '*' on Resource '*' violate least privilege. Scope: customer-managed policies that are attached to at least one identity (AWS-managed AdministratorAccess is not evaluated).
findings.expected_state: No attached customer-managed policy allows Action "*" on Resource "*"
remediation: Replace the policy with scoped permissions (use IAM Access Analyzer policy generation from CloudTrail activity).
Detach the over-permissive policy once replacements are in place.

CIS.title: Ensure IAM policies that allow full "*:*" administrative privileges are not attached

findings.title: IAM users receive permissions only through groups
findings.description: Direct user policies are hard to audit and tend to accumulate; group/role-based access is reviewable.
findings.expected_state: No managed or inline policies attached directly to IAM users
remediation: Create a group per job function and attach the policies to it.
Add the user to the group, then detach/delete the user's direct policies.

CIS.title: Ensure IAM users receive permissions only through groups
